analysis.title: Global Equity Strategy: Market Update, Anatomy of Momentum Crash, Leadership into 1Q27
key_insights: JPM sees the October 2026 selloff as a deleveraging event inside an intact AI cycle, not an end-of-cycle turn. Momentum (L/S) is down ~40% from its peak, the largest unwind since the post-GFC recovery. The S&P 500 target stays at 8,000.

Long Momentum (vs. market) fell 11% in October, about a 6 sigma move and the worst month in ~40 years. The Short leg rallied 5%, so Long/Short lost 16%. Quality and Growth had their worst months on record (-3.2z and -4.0z).

Momentum crowding fell from the 100th percentile to the 76th percentile vs 40 years of history, and is at the 43rd percentile vs 5 years. Low Vol crowding rose from the 0th to the 24th-25th percentile.

Positioning signals point to late-stage capitulation. Levered ETFs sold ~$60B on Nov 5 (2nd largest ever) and >$35B the prior Friday. CTAs are net short US equities. Vol-targeting leverage fell from the ~65th to the ~30th percentile, with ~$50B of equity still to sell. Dealer net gamma is in the ~12th percentile.

JPM reverses its cautious stance on Momentum and no longer calls it crowded. It recommends long 12-month Momentum (Semis, Tech Hardware) vs 3-month Momentum (Staples, Energy). It expects retail and institutional flows to return into year-end and early 2027.
Money market funds hold $7.9T as of October-end, up ~$500B over the past year. JPM expects price-sensitive retail and corporate cohorts to deploy this cash after the Momentum drawdown.

Low Vol is less compelling after crowding normalized from the 0th to the ~25th percentile. Best Low Vol sectors are Health Care, then Utilities, and least Staples. Low Vol would need a large rise in recession odds to keep outperforming (Polymarket puts next-year recession odds at 30%).

AI Upstream looks more attractive after the positioning flush, but the market wants clarity on trillion-dollar IPO(s), the ERCOT decision next month and oil/geopolitics ahead of the December FOMC. Hyperscalers have less short-term relative upside but room to re-rate over the medium term.

Equity multiples have de-rated ~4x since the January highs. The S&P 500 forward P/E fell ~3x since May, with index-level earnings revisions broadly flat. AI supply chain NTM P/E fell from 24.3x to 15.9x (-35%), semis -52%, hyperscalers -14%, memory -60%.

JPM expects 2027 hyperscaler capex of ~$1.7T (~$1.4T excl. SPCX) vs consensus of ~$1.3T, and ~$2.0T in 2028. It says 2027 capex will likely be at least ~$1.5T. Each $100B of extra capex adds ~$9 to S&P 500 EPS (~2.5% growth). JPM estimates 2027 EPS growth of ~20%.

AI 30 basket 2026 capex estimates were revised up ~$350B, from ~$580B to ~$930B. 2027 capex is expected above ~$1.3T (+40% y/y). AI capex has surprised estimates by ~29% on average since the start of 2024.

Hyperscaler buybacks have shrunk. LTM buybacks are ~$27B vs ~$103B at 3Q25, and only MSFT has repurchased this year. S&P 500 buyback announcements are a record ~$1.2T YTD (NVDA $230B, AAPL $100B, JPM $50B, WMT $30B, C $30B).

Post-midterm, JPM sees a Democratic sweep as a clearing event with better-than-feared political headwinds. It views a comprehensive federal AI regulation or national datacenter moratorium as unlikely. The binding constraints are now at the state level, and 42 of 45 local ballot measures restricting datacenters have passed or are leaning to pass.

JPM expects 2027 AI capex to be insulated because projects are already under construction and mostly funded, but the growth curve flattens ahead of 2028 as permitting gets harder. Moratoriums are expected to be temporary. Texas is a key test, with 27% of datacenter capacity funded in the HY project finance market.

The JPM Blue Wave basket (JPRBW26M) is up ~11% relative to the market since October. Hospitals rose +14.7%, Medicaid managed care +9.9%, municipal water +6.6%, application software +6.5%, and renewable-exposed utilities +6.2% in the 2 days after the midterms. The AI/Data Center/Electrification basket fell -16.2% and Aerospace & Defense -11.9% (Figure 33 shows these as 2-day moves).

Top 12M Momentum remains concentrated in Semis and Hardware and is highly correlated with AI upstream (correlation ~0.8). Flat performance in those names could rotate them out of the Momentum portfolio in 1H27, and quant rebalancing in 2Q27 would add selling pressure.
Asia Momentum crowding fell from the 95th to the 68th percentile, a smaller move than the July Asia-led unwind (100th to 56th percentile). Asia tech has led the US AI complex this year.

Affordability remains a hurdle for Consumer Cyclicals. Housing names would need mortgage rates near 6.0% for structural flows. Post-midterm, JPM prefers lower-ticket consumer exposure over names that depend on sharply lower rates.
QQQ RSI fell below 30 on Nov 5. In nine prior instances over three years, QQQ rallied ~4% on average over the next five trading days. Today's NFP added 165k jobs.

sector_views.rationale: Long 12M Momentum vs 3M Momentum after the positioning flush, though quant rebalancing in 2Q27 is a risk if the group trades sideways.
They are the 3M Momentum leg in the recommended long 12M vs 3M Momentum pair.
Best opportunity within Low Vol, helped by post-midterm Medicaid policy beneficiaries.
Second-best within Low Vol, and renewable-exposed utilities rose +6.2% after the midterms.
Less short-term relative upside, but attractive risk-reward and room to re-rate medium term as constrained compute supports pricing power and margins.
Affordability is a structural hurdle tied to oil, borrowing costs and housing shortage, with long-term value in retail, apparel and restaurants.
Long-term value, but structural flows need mortgage rates near 6.0%.
Would benefit if a lame-duck budget reconciliation package passes, though floor time may limit its scope.

earnings_insights: JPM estimates 2027 S&P 500 EPS growth of ~20% (JPM estimate). Consensus 2026 and 2027 EPS were revised up 9% and 12% in 1H26.
Index-level earnings revisions have been broadly flat since May (JPM data).
JPM estimates every $100B of 2027 hyperscaler capex adds ~$9 to S&P 500 EPS (~2.5% growth). Capex at ~$1.5T would add ~$18 of EPS vs consensus, or 4-5% to 2027 EPS growth.
The Earnings Momentum factor unwound sharply like Price Momentum, driven by Semis and Hardware exposure.
S&P 500 NTM P/E is 17.9x vs 21.2x in May. The AI supply chain NTM P/E is 15.9x vs 24.3x.

trade_ideas.risk: Quant rebalancing in 2Q27 could push AI upstream names out of the top Momentum portfolio if they trade sideways.

trade_ideas.description: Reduce emphasis on Low Vol relative to Momentum, keeping Health Care, then Utilities, as preferred Low Vol exposure
trade_ideas.rationale: Low Vol crowding normalized from the 0th to ~25th percentile and the economic cycle remains intact.
trade_ideas.risk: A large increase in recession odds would drive Low Vol to outperform.

trade_ideas.description: Hyperscalers as a medium-term re-rating opportunity
trade_ideas.rationale: Constrained compute capacity could support pricing power, incremental margins and operating cash flow, attracting long-only investors.
trade_ideas.risk: Hyperscaler negative free cash flow and delayed monetization could push leverage higher.

risk_factors: Further deleveraging: ~$50B of vol-targeting selling remains, CTAs are net short and dealer gamma support has faded.
Geopolitical re-escalation in the Middle East and the path of oil, which could affect the December FOMC.
Financial conditions have tightened ahead of the December Fed decision.
State-level datacenter moratoriums and permitting delays could flatten the AI capex curve ahead of 2028.
Texas ERCOT decision next month could change how the forward AI capex curve is modeled.
Trillion-dollar mega-cap IPO(s) could absorb liquidity.
Hyperscaler negative free cash flow and funding needs, with the funding mix needing more equity participation.
Momentum quant rebalancing in 2Q27 if Semis and Hardware trade sideways.
Consumer affordability pressure from oil, borrowing costs and the housing shortage.
Federal policy constraints: the Senate 60-vote filibuster threshold and presidential veto limit legislative change, and executive action remains a source of market risk.

vol_and_positioning: Levered ETFs sold ~$60B on Nov 5 (2nd largest in history) and >$35B the prior Friday into the close, bringing exposure below beginning-of-year levels.
CTAs have turned net short US equities. Vol-targeting target leverage fell from ~65th to ~30th percentile, with ~$50B of equity exposure left to sell over the coming days.
Dealer net gamma imbalance is in the ~12th percentile and the long-gamma support has subsided. Risks are two-way.
Momentum crowding is at the 76th percentile vs 40 years (0th, 5th and 43rd percentile vs 1, 3 and 5 years). Low Vol crowding is at the 24th percentile.
Asia Momentum crowding is at the 66.6th percentile and EM Momentum crowding is at the 41.4th percentile as of Nov 6.
JPM's broad leverage index recorded its largest deleveraging since the 2022 post-Covid bust, larger than Liberation Day. Equity long/short leverage fell sharply per the JPM Prime Desk.
Corporate buybacks of $1.2T announced YTD are expected to continue to support the market.
Momentum fell 3% vs the market on Thursday (-7.9z). Growth and Forward Growth also underperformed by 3% (-8.8z and -7.4z).
geopolitical: Potential developments in the Middle East and the path of oil are named as catalysts that could affect the December FOMC.
JPM cannot fully discount a geopolitical re-escalation despite the recent drop in oil prices.
A Ukraine cease-fire basket (JPEUUKRN) outperformed after the midterms.
Midterm results: a broad Democratic sweep across House, Senate, governor and state legislative races.
The President retains influence over trade, tariffs, geopolitics, sanctions and regulation through executive action.

tension_points.theme: AI momentum unwind: reset or cycle end
tension_points.bull_case: JPM sees an intra-cycle deleveraging event: crowding has normalized, positioning is washed out, buybacks are at a record, 2027 EPS growth is ~20% and the S&P 500 target is 8,000.
tension_points.bear_case: Equity multiples have de-rated ~4x, vol-targeting funds still have ~$50B to sell, CTAs are net short, dealer gamma support has faded, and datacenter regulation and funding constraints could flatten the capex curve.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Significant downward revisions to 2027 earnings, which would signal end-cycle dynamics and leave capitulation further to run.

tension_points.bull_case: Momentum crowding is no longer extreme and flows should return into year-end, favoring long 12M Momentum (Semis, Hardware).
tension_points.bear_case: A large rise in recession risk would keep Low Vol outperforming, and 12M Momentum names could rotate out in 1H27 if they trade sideways.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A large increase in recession odds, currently 30% for next year per Polymarket.
